To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The emergence of communication is facilitated when agents are placed in a social context and are able to form categories from the environment.

the evolution of communication abilities in an artificial environment depends on the presence of a social group and the ability to categorize the environment, and that the evolution of a communication ability depends on the presence and the nature of other abilities.

(1) the ability to form and maintain social relationships with conspecifics is necessary for the emergence of communication and language; (2) the ability to categorize objects and to form categories from experience with an environment is necessary for the development of communication and language abilities; and (3) the ability to learn from social interactions is important to communication and language development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of communication and the emergence of language.
the emergence of communication and language in a population of autonomous agents that are situated in a shared environment.
understanding the evolution of communication and its relation to other cognitive and social abilities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
communication is not a necessary component of a complex system, but that it may be a beneficial one.

the emergence of communication is a function of a number of factors including the environment, the nature of the task, the nature of communication itself, the nature of social interactions, and the nature of the agents.
the emergence of communication is a consequence of social interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ability to categorize the world, and to form a mental lexicon of categories, constitutes the ground for evolution of language.
social interactions are necessary but not sufficient for the emergence of linguistic communication.
social and cognitive abilities, in particular the ability to form and categorize, are crucial in the development of communication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emergence of communication is a complex and subtle process that requires an understanding of the role of social, evolutionary, and cognitive factors.
the evolution of communication is not a single event.
the emergence of communication in a group of robots depends on the interplay between social and evolutionary factors.
